subject: Maths
title: Year 9 Maths Exam 3
intro: You may use a calculator, but show your working in the working box: a calculator answer with no working may score nothing. Give answers to the accuracy asked for.

questions.q: Which inequality has the solution x < −2?
questions.ms: B1: −3x > 6. Dividing by −3 reverses the sign, giving x < −2.

questions.q: Simplify 5x(x − 2) − 3x2.
What are the solutions of 4x2 − 25 = 0?
A quadratic graph crosses the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 6. What is the x-coordinate of its turning point?
questions.ms: B1: 2, midway between −2 and 6.

questions.q: n is an integer such that 2n − 3 > −7 and 3n ≤ 12. Write down all the possible values of n.
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. M1 for n > −2. M1 for n ≤ 4. A1 for the list.

questions.q: Solve 2x + 53 ≥ x − 1.
questions.hint: Type it like x>4 or -2<x<=3 (use <= for ≤ and >= for ≥)
questions.ms: Answer: x ≤ 8. M1 for 2x + 5 ≥ 3(x − 1). M1 for collecting terms, e.g. 8 ≥ x. A1 for x ≤ 8.

questions.q: (Challenge) Expand and simplify (x + 4)(x − 3)(x + 2).
questions.ms: Answer: x³ + 3x² − 10x − 24. M1 for x² + x − 12. M1 for multiplying by (x + 2) with at least 4 correct terms. A1.

questions.q: Factorise fully 2x2 − 18.
Factorise 6x2 + x − 2.
questions.ms: Answer: (2x − 1)(3x + 2). M1 for 6x² + 4x − 3x − 2, or brackets giving two correct terms. A1.

questions.q:
Aisha is solving x(x + 5) = 2(x + 5). She says:
"I can divide both sides by (x + 5), so x = 2 is the only solution."
Is Aisha correct? You must show your working.
questions.ms: Answer: not correct, x = 2 or x = −5. M1 for x² + 3x − 10 = 0 oe. A1 for both solutions. C1 for explaining that dividing by (x + 5) loses x = −5.

questions.q: Solve 2x2 − 3x − 7 = 0. Give your answers to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 2.77 or x = −1.27. M1 for correct substitution into the formula. M1 for √65. A1 for both.

questions.q:
A model rocket is launched straight up. Its height, h metres, after t seconds is given by h = 40t − 5t2.
After how many seconds does the rocket land?
questions.ms: Answer: 8 seconds. M1 for 5t(8 − t) = 0 oe. A1.

questions.q: For how long is the rocket at least 60 m above the ground? (seconds)
questions.ms: Answer: 4 seconds. M1 for t² − 8t + 12 = 0 oe. M1 for t = 2 and t = 6. A1 for 6 − 2 = 4.

questions.q: Work out the maximum height of the rocket. (metres)
questions.ms: Answer: 80 m. M1 for t = 4 (midway between 0 and 8). A1.

questions.q:
A lift can carry a maximum of 600 kg. Four people already in the lift weigh 72 kg, 85 kg, 68 kg and 91 kg. Two more people, each weighing w kg, want to get in with a 52 kg suitcase.
Write an inequality in terms of w.
questions.hint: Type it like x>4 or -2<x<=3 (use <= for ≤ and >= for ≥)

questions.q: Solve your inequality.
questions.hint: Type it like x>4 or -2<x<=3 (use <= for ≤ and >= for ≥)
questions.ms: Answer: w ≤ 116. M1 for 2w ≤ 232. A1.

questions.q: Instead, two brothers weighing 110 kg and 125 kg want to get in with the suitcase. Can they both get in? Show how you decide.
questions.ms: Answer: No. C1: 368 + 110 + 125 = 603 kg, which is more than 600 kg (needs the total and a conclusion).

questions.q: Lina chooses an integer. She multiplies it by 3 and then subtracts 14. Her answer is at least 25 but less than 40. Work out all the integers Lina could have chosen.
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. P1 for 25 ≤ 3n − 14 < 40. M1 for 39 ≤ 3n < 54. A1 for 13 ≤ n < 18. A1 for the list.

questions.q:
A triangle has base (x + 3) cm and perpendicular height 2x cm. Its area is 54 cm2.
Show that x2 + 3x − 54 = 0.
Work out the base and the height of the triangle.
questions.hint: Type the base then the height, like 5,8
questions.ms: Answer: base 9 cm, height 12 cm. M1 for (x + 9)(x − 6) = 0. A1 for x = 6 (reject −9). A1 for both dimensions.

questions.q: Solve x2 + 2x − 10 > 0. Give the values in your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: Type it like x<-1 or x>4 (use <= for ≤ and >= for ≥)
questions.ms: Answer: x < −4.32 or x > 2.32. M1 for the formula with a = 1, b = 2, c = −10. A1 for −4.32 and 2.32. M1 for a sketch or reasoning that the curve is above zero outside the roots. A1 for the correct regions.

questions.q: Prove that the sum of the squares of any two consecutive integers is always odd.
questions.ms: M1 for n² + (n + 1)². A1 for 2n² + 2n + 1. C1 for 2(n² + n) + 1 is one more than an even number, so odd. Number examples alone score 0.
